sections.html:
Owners here pick between an agent listing, a sale on their own and a cash offer. Which one fits depends on the house's condition and your calendar. The city lies in central Oklahoma, with Norman on its southern border and Oklahoma City hugging the other three sides. It is still its own municipality. Permits, code complaints and utility accounts for a Moore address go through Moore's own offices.

Population was 62,793 in 2020 and is estimated at 63,609 for July 2025. The city annexed 21.6 square miles in 1961 and became a full city in 1962, and much of the housing dates from the years after. Three questions dominate: must storm damage be repaired first, was the shelter or addition permitted, and how quickly can closing happen.

Many Moore buyers open with tornado history, so have straight answers ready. Significant tornadoes struck on October 4, 1998, May 3, 1999, May 8, 2003, May 10, 2010 and May 20, 2013, with weaker ones on May 31, 2013 and March 25, 2015. The 1999 storm was rated F5 and its damage path ran more than a mile wide at times. The 2013 storm was rated EF5, hit Briarwood and Plaza Towers elementary schools while classes were in session and killed 24 people.

In practical terms:

  • A shelter or safe room adds appeal when it was permitted. The city requires a permit, and the inspections division takes applications at City Hall.
  • Before listing, ask Inspections whether the city can confirm that a shelter is registered with emergency management.
  • The state's SoonerSafe program has offered safe room rebates through FEMA grants, so find out whether anyone claimed one on your property.
  • Roof and window repairs after hail or wind are common. File the invoices and permits together to show what was done and when.

Most remodels, additions and improvements need a building permit, as does all new construction. Not sure about your project? Call Inspections at 405-793-5051. Permits and inspections run through the city's GovBuilt portal, and same-day inspections are possible when you call or message through the portal before 9 a.m. Inspectors work from the 2018 International Residential Code, the 2018 International Property Maintenance Code and the 2020 National Electric Code, with local and state amendments.

Unpermitted work is where sales stall. Lenders and inspectors sometimes request records for a converted garage, a fence, a patio slab or a shelter set into a garage floor. A separate code enforcement desk at the same address, 405-793-5052, handles weeds, debris and maintenance complaints.

Hot summers, frequent hail and the occasional flash flood take a toll. A buyer's inspector usually starts with:

  • Roof age, shingle condition and hail marks
  • Window and garage door damage
  • Drainage around the foundation after heavy rain
  • Attic and ceiling stains from past leaks

Repair records carry weight. After a claim-funded roof replacement, the paperwork can matter more to a buyer than the shingles.

Cleveland County's assessor sets the value and its treasurer collects. A bill may be paid in two parts: pay half by December 31 and the remainder is due by March 31, but an unpaid bill on December 31 turns delinquent.

Ask the title company, ahead of signing, for the payoff figure, any open permits and where the taxes stand. Those three answers prevent most surprises.

If you sell a one- or two-unit property, state law (60 O.S. section 831 and the sections after it, the Residential Property Condition Disclosure Act) has you hand the buyer a condition disclosure or a disclaimer. The Oklahoma Real Estate Commission publishes the form. Disclosing a defect you know about, such as old storm damage, limits your later liability for it under section 835. Unsure how to answer a line? Ask a real estate attorney.

Moore Public Schools covers more than the city limits, and some addresses with a Moore or nearby mailing name fall in other districts, so confirm the district for an address instead of assuming it from the mailing name.

If a past storm damaged the house, buyers will ask what was repaired, what was replaced and what was left. Have a short written list with dates, the contractor's name, the insurance claim result and the permits issued. Photos from before and after the work help a lot, and so do any warranty papers for the new roof or windows. Anything still open, for example a pending claim or a repair not finished, belongs on the disclosure form before an offer is accepted.

A seller who volunteers this early usually keeps the sale on track. A buyer who finds it at inspection tends to ask for a lower price or walk.

Whichever buyer you choose, a title company closes the deal. It confirms who owns the house, looks for liens and tax balances, and prepares the deed and the settlement statement. Read that statement line by line before closing day. It should show your payoff, the tax share and anything else deducted.

With a cash sale there is no lender appraisal and no loan commitment, so the closing date depends mostly on how fast the title work clears and when you want to move. You hand over keys, garage door openers and any shelter or warranty paperwork. If the house is vacant, shut off nothing until the closing is complete, and switch utility accounts into the buyer's name afterward through Moore's offices.

Each calls for a different route; cash is only one.

  • Storm or hail damage that is unrepaired, with an insurance claim still open
  • An inherited house whose heirs live elsewhere and want a clean sale
  • A rental with a tenant, deferred maintenance or a city code notice
  • A shelter, addition or garage conversion with no permit on file
  • A short timeline from a move, a job change or a mortgage problem

Cash buyers accept the property as it stands, so the leaking roof and dated kitchen stay unfixed. The price accounts for that. Weigh it against the likely net of repairing and listing, after fees and months on the market, and get any buyer's terms on paper.

faqs.q: Is Moore, Oklahoma part of Oklahoma City?
faqs.a: No. Moore is its own incorporated city in Cleveland County, although Oklahoma City surrounds it on the north, east and west. Permits, code enforcement and utilities for a Moore address go through the City of Moore.

faqs.q: Do I need a permit record to sell a house with a storm shelter in Moore?
faqs.a: Moore requires a permit for a storm shelter, and buyers or their lenders may ask for it. Call Inspections at 405-793-5051 to see what is on file, and ask whether the shelter is registered with emergency management.

faqs.q: When are property taxes due in Cleveland County?
faqs.a: They can be paid in full or in halves. At least half must be paid by December 31 to avoid delinquency, and the second half is due by March 31.

faqs.q: Do I have to disclose tornado damage when I sell in Moore?
faqs.a: Oklahoma law has sellers of one or two dwelling units give the buyer a disclosure or disclaimer statement. If you know of a defect such as past storm damage, put it on the form.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Moore house as-is for cash?
faqs.a: Yes. A cash buyer can purchase a house in its current condition, and owners often choose this when repairs, probate or timing make a listing hard. Compare offers and get the terms in writing.
